mirage_vs: Variant-set level analysis

Source: R/api.R
mirage_vs.Rd

Variant-level rare variant association test using a Bayesian mixture model.

Usage

mirage_vs(
  data,
  n1,
  n2,
  gamma = 3,
  sigma = 2,
  eta.init = 0.1,
  estimate.eta = TRUE,
  fixed_eta = NULL,
  max.iter = 10000L,
  tol = 1e-05,
  verbose = TRUE
)

Arguments

data

Data frame with columns: ID, No.case, No.contr, category. A 3-column input (without ID) is accepted with a warning.

n1

Sample size in cases.

n2

Sample size in controls.

gamma

Prior mean of the relative-risk parameter. Scalar or length-K vector.

sigma

Prior rate of the relative-risk parameter. Scalar or length-K vector. The Gamma prior has shape gamma * sigma and scale 1 / sigma.

eta.init

Initial value for proportion of risk variants.

estimate.eta

Logical. Whether to estimate eta.

fixed_eta

Numeric vector of fixed eta values (required when estimate.eta = FALSE). Must have length K.

max.iter

Maximum EM iterations.

tol

Convergence tolerance.

verbose

Logical. Print progress messages.

Value

An object of class mirage_vs_result.

Examples

toy <- data.frame(
  ID = c("v1", "v2", "v3", "v4"),
  No.case = c(3L, 1L, 0L, 2L),
  No.contr = c(1L, 0L, 2L, 0L),
  category = c(1L, 2L, 1L, 2L)
)
mirage_vs(toy, n1 = 500, n2 = 500, verbose = FALSE)
#> 
#> ── MIRAGE Variant-Set Analysis Result ──────────────────────────────────────────
#> Number of variants analyzed: 4
#> Number of variant categories: 2
#> 
#> ── Category-specific risk proportions (eta) ──
#> 
#>  category      eta.est eta.pvalue
#>         1 0.0001999959  1.0000000
#>         2 1.0000000000  0.1323021
